builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MedUIGym: Evaluating and Training GUI Agents for Clinical Workflows
summary: MedUIGym replaces ad hoc, text-only evaluation of clinical GUI agents with a unified interactive environment of 15,739 tasks spanning six clinical task families, dual GUI/native-tool interfaces, and verified final answers and actions. The cost to the reader is substantial: meaningful use requires running or hosting EHR sandbox infrastructure, collecting parallel GUI trajectories, and, for the training results, fine-tuning and RL over vision-language models at a scale that exceeds a single 24 GB GPU without external APIs. What can fail is transfer: the headline finding is that twelve current vision-language models struggle on these workflows and that increased reasoning effort yields no consistent gains, so even successful in-domain training may not translate into reliable production behavior on real, non-sandbox EHR systems with different layouts and latency characteristics.
rationale: The paper contributes an evaluation and training environment rather than a deployable efficiency technique, and its findings are negative results that carry no quantified gain the reader could exploit directly.
technique: Interactive benchmark and training gym for clinical GUI agents
